content.text: : resp droplets · contact w contaminated surface · person-to-person contact · airborne (stays airborne ≤2h) - highly contagious
contagious ~5d b4 rash → 4d after - most pts Sxtomatic
RF: unvaccinated young child - leading cause of mortality in children <5y worldwide
· malaise · irritability · photophobia - USU lasts 2-4d - fever persists ~5-7d

: sm red spots w white centers on oral mucosa - white or gray elevations on buccal mucosa - appear ~48h b4 exanthem - pathognomonic - sm irregular spots w white (or blue) center on palatal or buccal mucosa opposite molars - last 1-4d
•starts on face & behind ears - pinhead-sized papules coalesce → brick red irregular maculopapular rash → trunk & extremities
•± tonsillar exudate · pharyngeal erythema · gen LAD · splenomegaly
ddx Fordyce spots: visible sebaceous glands - skin-colored · white or red - mouth · genitals · face - ⍉assoc w measles or other infect
Dx clinical - nasopharyngeal PCR = definitive - IgM measles Ab (ELISA) or 4-fold ↑ serum hemagglutination inhibition Ab supports dx
prevention = best tx - live MMR or MMRV vax
for young/severely malnourished children - boosts immune response - ↓ risk of comp & death - give if signs of vit A deficiency · severe sxs · child <2y - ↓pediatric morbidity & mortality
*can suppress immune system for 6wks → otitis media · bact PNA
•⍉teratogenic - infect in preg → spont abortion & perinatal mortality
: type IV (delayed) hypersensitivity rxn to pyrogenic strain (erythrogenic toxin A, B, C)
aka scarlatina - S. pyogenes (group A β-hemolytic strep)
typically w.in 2d of acute strep pharyngitis (w.in 1wk of sore throat)
MC in children 3-14y - Hx of untx GAS infect = strong RF for scarlet fever & rheumatic Hdz
•strep pharyngitis: fever · ⍉cough · anterior cervical LAD · pharyngeal erythema · tonsillar exudates · abd pain
•spreads rapidly → desquamates - sm (1-2mm) papules - rash resolves w.in 1wk - desquamation may last several more wks
Flushed face w circumoral pallor & strawberry tongue
strawberry tongue: diffusely erythematous beefy-red tongue w prominently hypertrophied papillae
seen @ P points · axillary · antecubital · abd or inguinal areas
*rash on palms/soles: syphilis · measles · RMSF · toxic shock syndrome · bact endocarditis (Janeway lesions) · reactive arthritis · Kawasaki · meningococcemia · HFMD
Dx: characteristic rash + hx of strep infect
- children: PO penicillin V or amoxicillin x10d - same tx as strep pharyngitis - ⍉additional tx for rash - amoxicillin preferred in children (more palatable) · penicillin in adults
- may return to school 24h after starting abx
- abx indicated (⍉supportive care alone) → hasten sx resolution & ↓risk of rheumatic fever (♡ valve damage)
: ↑risk of acute rheumatic fever · poststrep GN
: resp droplets - inhalation of lrg particle aerosols → prolonged & close contact needed
pre-vax: outbreaks every few yrs w peaks in winter & early spring - MC school-age children
many cases aSx - sore throat · HA - low-grade fever concurrent w or ≤5d b4 rash
PE: prominent posterior cervical · posterior auricular · occipital LAD
spreads much more rapidly than measles - does ⍉darken/coalesce
•appears 14-17d postexposure - face → trunk & extremities w.in 24h - minimal systemic sxs
: pinpoint red macules & petechiae on soft palate & uvula
arthralgias/arthritis in ≤70% of teens & adult women
ddx erysipelas: β-hemolytic strep (GAS = S. pyogenes)
Rubella-specific IgM Ab via EIA - test of choice - detectable as early as 4d after rash & persists ≥6-8wks
•US: only available as MMR (live-attenuated) - goal = prevent maternal infect → congenital rubella syndrome
•can still occur after vax ← inapprop initial response or waning immunity
– infects & destroys retic → ↓ or transient halt in erythropoiesis - nonenveloped linear ssDNA virus
prevention: handwashing · ⍉close contact · ⍉sharing food or drinks
also N/D · coryza · sore throat · cough · conjunctivitis - URI sxs 3-4d b4 rash - prodromal sxs resolve by time reticular rash appears
in older children/adults (adults > children) - sm joints of hands & ft ± rash
•2-5d after prodrome: erythematous malar rash w circumoral pallor - most prominent on face/cheeks → several days later reticulated (lace-like) rash on trunk & extremities
Dx clinical w classic sxs & malar rash - serology only if atypical presentation & would alt mgnt (ex, new-onset arthropathy)
aplastic anemia → NAAT detects parvovirus B19
: acetaminophen · NSAIDs - uncomp = self-limited - prodrome resolves w.in few days · rash w.in few wks - NSAIDs for arthritis/arthralgias
in pts w sickle cell - other comp: meningitis · encephalitis · deafness · myocarditis · pancreatitis

*transient aplastic crisis: destroys erythrocyte progenitors → ↓retic → severe anemia in RBC dx (sickle cell · thalassemia · hereditary spherocytosis · IDA) → RBC transfusion - good prognosis (resolves in days-wks)
*IS pts → pure red cell aplasia → severe chronic anemia
*maternal infect → fetal anemia · cardiomegaly · hydrops fetalis · growth restriction
: resp droplets · saliva - postnatal via saliva · prenatal via placenta
all seasons - most cases w.o known exposure
aka exanthem subitum · sixth dz · pseudorubella · exanthem criticum · 3-day fever
HHV-6 ⍉teratogenic - perinatal transmission rare (~1%) - congenital infect aSx - postnatal infect → acute febrile illness
– child appears well during febrile phase -
only viral exanthem that starts on the trunk
•rash in child on abx can mimic drug allergy
± irritability · diarrhea · bulging fontanel · conjunctivitis · URI sxs (cough · rhinorrhea)
: drug eruption · rubella · rubeola · scarlet fever · 5th dz · enteroviral infect
Viral cx/PCR for confirmation - labs seldom needed
CBC: relative neutropenia · mild atypical lymphocytosis · thrombocytopenia - UA: sterile pyuria
*infant w ↑fever + rash + bulging fontanel → consider meningitis
•prevention: hand hygiene - sporadic cases ⍉contagious - ⍉exclusion from daycare/school
: antivirals (ganciclovir) - ganciclovir or foscarnet also for comp infect (encephalitis · myocarditis)
- roseola = major cause of febrile sz in children - HHV-6 (B-cell lymphotropic) also assoc w encephalitis · Hashimoto thyroiditis · myocarditis · acute liver failure
